# Bioterrorists
A bioterror cell is a covert team antagonist that builds its threat during the round. The cell begins together on an off-station infiltration vessel with no ready-to-release pathogen. Your advantage is a portable clandestine laboratory, limited supplies, and a private radio channel.
## Cell roles
Every cell has exactly one [bold]Head Bioterrorist[/bold]. The head receives the deployment duffel and is responsible for distributing equipment, choosing a hidden laboratory site, and coordinating the cell. If no preferred head is available, a regular Bioterrorist is promoted; the head slot does not remain empty.
Other [bold]Bioterrorists[/bold] collect samples, operate the laboratory, acquire replacement reagents, manufacture payloads, and infiltrate the station. All members share the bioterror radio channel.
## Establishing the laboratory
The head's deployment duffel contains three flatpacks:
- An [bold]environmental sample analyzer[/bold]. - A [bold]culture incubator[/bold]. - A [bold]pathogen synthesizer[/bold].
Use the supplied [bold]multitool[/bold] on each flatpack to deploy it. Establish the machines away from your starting vessel, somewhere with power and enough privacy to control an accident. The machines are contraband and can be destroyed, disassembled, or seized.
## Environmental sampling
Use a sterile environmental scraper on suitable sources such as walls, maintenance grime, vents, scrubbers, drains, refuse, soil, blood, and contaminated surfaces. Sampling takes time and can be interrupted. Sources have cooldowns and finite useful material.
A clean scraper produces better samples. Reusing a dirty scraper lowers quality and can cross-contaminate the result. Different environments offer different chassis and traits: vents favor airborne traits, waste favors ingestion, and dirty surfaces favor persistence or contact transmission.
## Analyzer, incubator, synthesizer
1. Insert a microbial sample into the [bold]analyzer[/bold] to identify its chassis, quality, contamination, and available traits. 2. Put the analyzed sample into the [bold]incubator[/bold]. It consumes culture nutrient and power to produce a viable culture. 3. Load a chassis culture and desired trait cultures into the [bold]synthesizer[/bold], add stabilizer, then begin synthesis.
Traits have a limited budget and some combinations are incompatible. A strain cannot maximize transmission, lethality, persistence, stealth, and resistance simultaneously.
## Containment
Power loss, dirty samples, invalid synthesis, or unattended cultures can ruin inputs and contaminate the machine, nearby surfaces, and local air. Wear sealed PPE, keep sterilizine available, and do not place the laboratory where one accident exposes the whole cell.
Medical scrubbers, sterilization, diagnosis, immunity, and vaccines all work against custom strains. Once Medical obtains a valid sample, it can identify your strain and manufacture a matching vaccine.
## Physical deployment
Synthesized strains are dispensed as physical cultures. They are not innate antagonist powers:
- Culture ampoules contaminate food or compatible surfaces. - Surface applicators spread contact-focused cultures. - Aerosol canisters release pathogen load into the local tile atmosphere.
Payload strength depends on culture concentration. Anyone can use a payload, but an unprotected operator risks exposure. Preserve a viable master culture and avoid revealing the laboratory before the cell can recover from a failed deployment.
## Objectives
The cell's shared goals include establishing all three machines away from the infiltration vessel, synthesizing a viable custom strain, deploying enough infectious load, delaying a confirmed diagnosis or vaccine, and keeping at least one member alive.
